title: How Steve Jobs launched "Think Different": getting Apple back to basics (1997 speech)
summary: Weeks after returning to Apple, Jobs explains the turnaround: cut 70% of the product roadmap, simplify distribution, and rebuild the brand around values rather than specs. He introduces the "Think Different" campaign, citing Nike and "Got Milk?" as models of marketing that conveys who a company is, not what its product does.

principles.text: Turn around a company by returning to basics: great products, great marketing, great distribution.
principles.quote: We’re trying to get back to the basics of great products, great marketing, and great distribution.

principles.text: Cut the product line hard; lack of focus confuses customers and your own team.
principles.quote: We actually got rid of 70 percent of the stuff on the product road map.

principles.text: Simplify the product line so customers can understand it, then make it better.
principles.quote: You’re going to see the product line get much simpler, and you’re going to see the product line get much better.

principles.text: Don't guess demand months ahead; strip out inventory and let customers tell you what they want.
principles.quote: So what we’re going to do is get really simple and start taking inventory out of those pipelines so we can let the customer tell us what they want, and we can respond to it super fast.

principles.text: Marketing is about values, not specs; in a noisy world be clear on the few things you want people to remember.
principles.quote: To me, marketing is about values. This is a very complicated world. It’s a very noisy world, and we’re not gonna get a chance to get people to remember much about us.

principles.text: Great brands don't sell product features; they honor what they stand for, as Nike does. Even great brands need ongoing investment.
principles.quote: What does Nike do in their advertising? They honor great athletes, and they honor great athletics. That’s who they are. That’s what they are about.
